newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices slide on new crop arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices slide on new crop arrivals.

text.p: Indian cotton prices fell on Wednesday on low mill buying and higher new crop arrivals, dealers said.

Cotton Corporation of India buying eased which in turn subdued sentiment. In spot deals Bengal-deshi fell by five rupees to 840/870 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 10/25 rupees to 1,450/1,650 rupees.

Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) fell by 100-300 to 18,000/18,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). "New crop arrivals in the Punjab region were about 25,000 bales (170 kg each) today while the offtake was about 10-12,000 bales," one broker said.
